angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 19,464,295 km at 111.98 pc = 2.32 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112440: distance 111.982 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.027), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 111.982 +/- 3.024 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.5987 +/- 0.3160 mas (same row, RUWE 4.15), 27.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 27.978 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112440: radius 27.978 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 379.591 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.058) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 19,464,295 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4820 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112440: effective temperature 4820 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.102) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112440: effective temperature 4820 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.102) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * lam Peg: spectral type G8IIIaCN0.5 (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * lam Peg: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * lam Peg: projected rotation speed 7.5 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 215665) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.12 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 16 published values span log g 1.75 to 3.2, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.4% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...682A.145S)
